text:
jessica: Hey - running into a 400 from the tool_call endpoint when I call invoice_tool. Error says 'invalid JSON' but the body looks fine to me, pasted curl below. Any idea?

jessica: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tool_call \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{invoiceId: 123, notes: 'Reviewed by QA', patterns: [/^INV-\d+$/], }'
```

alex: Can you share the raw request body exactly as sent (no screenshots)? Also, what's the SDK/client you used?

jessica: pasted exact - I used a quick curl copy from a colleague's node script. I didn't run JSON.stringify - just copied the object literal.

support-bot: Automated note: Request failed schema validation - parser threw UnexpectedToken at position 12.

alex: Yup — that body is a JS object literal, not valid JSON. Problems I see: keys not double-quoted (invoiceId), single quotes around string, trailing comma after the array, and a RegExp literal (/^INV-\d+$/) which JSON doesn't support.

jessica: omg, facepalm. Is that something the API can detect and give a clearer message for? The error is just 'invalid JSON' which wasn't actionable.

tim: From eng side, can we detect common patterns (unquoted keys, single-quoted strings, regex literal) and return a hint like: "keys must be double-quoted; strings must use ""; remove regex literals or stringify them"? Current parser just bubbles up UnexpectedToken.

maria: Agree — small parser pre-check would help reduce support churn. I can add a lightweight heuristic that checks for unquoted keys ("[A-Za-z0-9_]+:" absence) and common JS literal tokens (/, /\*) and suggest corrections. Will open a PR.

alex: For this user, quick fix: replace body with valid JSON. Example: ```
{
  "invoiceId": 123,
  "notes": "Reviewed by QA",
  "patterns": ["^INV-\\d+$"]
}
```
Use -d '$(jq -c . payload.json)' or echo -n '...json...' to avoid shell single-quote conflicts.

jessica: That fixed it, thanks. Also, can you add a short note in the docs about common mistakes (JS object literal, regexes, trailing commas)? I can link the support thread.

alex: Will do. Filing docs ticket and adding a quickline in the error troubleshooting page. Ticket: DOCS-789.

maria: PR for parser hints drafted, assigning to tim for review. We'll include tests with sample bad payloads (unquoted keys, single quotes, regex literal).

tim: Thanks — once merged we'll also tweak the 400 body to include the detection hint.

jessica: Appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:

support-bot: Thread closed after resolution.
